The FEHA (Fair Employment and Housing Act) and the ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) have several differences.

Americans on the no-fly list will now be given information about why they have been banned from commercial flights and the chance to dispute their status, according to court documents filed by the Justice Department.
This change comes in response to a ruling by a federal judge in June that said the old process was in violation of the Fifth Amendment's guarantee of due process.
The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), who brought the lawsuit on behalf of 13 Americans on the list, is not satisfied with the new policy.
They argue that the government's redress process does not meet constitutional requirements because it denies individuals meaningful notice, evidence, and a hearing.
